_comment: Every finding, tagged with the ONE module it belongs to. docs/build-module-pages.mjs turns this into one page per module. Findings were being written into whichever page was open at the time, so Patients and Laboratory ended up sharing a page and a combined 'all problems' page mixed six modules together. A finding now has exactly one home, and the pages are generated rather than edited.

severities.critical: money, data loss or patient safety

findings.title: The commission amount comes from the browser
findings.detail: Whatever commissionAmount the client sends is what gets stored. The server does not recompute it from the doctor's fee slab.
findings.proof: reproduced against the running controller — backend/scripts/doctor-acct-probe.mjs
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md rule 3 — never trust a price the client sent

findings.title: Another hospital's fee configuration can be written
findings.detail: The fee-slab write is not tenant-guarded, so a doctorId belonging to a different organisation is accepted and stored.
findings.proof: reproduced — a cross-tenant id was written and read back
findings.rule: CLAUDE.md rule 4 — every id in the body is hostile until proven to belong to this tenant

findings.title: “Settled” reports how many were asked for, not how many settled
findings.detail: Send ten commissions to settle, three succeed, and the response says ten. The count comes from the request array, never from the write result.
findings.proof: reproduced — 10 requested, 3 rows changed, response said 10

findings.title: ?resource=stats ships passwordHash and invitationToken to the browser
findings.detail: About 2 MB, and it carries both secrets in every row. The ?resource=doctors endpoint was narrowed earlier; this one was never touched.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log
findings.retraction: This module was reported earlier as “3.2 MB → 552 KB, fixed”. The live log says 564 KB for doctors and ~2 MB for stats. It got smaller; it was not fixed.

findings.title: Expired batches still dispense
findings.detail: Nothing checks the expiry date at the point of issue, so stock past its date is handed over.
findings.proof: reproduced inside a rolled-back transaction — backend/scripts/pharmacy-dispense-probe.mjs

findings.title: The remaining quantity is silently discarded on a partial dispense
findings.detail: When a batch cannot cover the full quantity, the shortfall is dropped rather than drawn from the next batch or refused.
findings.proof: same probe

findings.title: /api/pharmacy/stats takes 574–1,204 ms to return 375 bytes
findings.detail:
A tiny answer that takes that long is a query problem, not a payload one — whatever it aggregates has no index.

Re-verified 10 August. Re-measured 226 ms (runs 211/226/228). See PERF-REVERIFY.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: A critical finding can be filed with nobody told
findings.detail: criticalNotifiedTo and criticalNotifiedAt both exist and are both optional. “Acute bleed — immediate neurosurgical review required” can be stored with the record stating that nobody was informed.
findings.proof: reproduced — 200 OK with hasCriticalFindings true and both notify fields null
findings.rule: This is the failure radiology departments are audited on, and the schema was designed for it

findings.title: A report cannot be corrected — the second one returns 500
findings.detail: RadiologyReport.orderId is @unique, so one study carries exactly one report. Issuing a corrected one violates the constraint and the error is unhandled.
findings.proof: reproduced — 500 on the second report for the same study

findings.title: The caller chooses whose name is on the report
findings.detail: reportedById is taken from the request body. The server knows who is logged in and does not use it.
findings.proof: reproduced — asked for Dr Aryan Verma, stored Dr Aryan Verma

findings.title: An empty report is accepted, and takes the only slot
findings.detail: Every field except orderId is optional. Combined with RA2, that empty row becomes the only report the study will ever have.
findings.proof: reproduced

findings.title: Nothing checks pregnancy or contrast allergy before a scan
findings.detail: Allergies ARE recorded — the test patient carries ["Penicillin","Dust"] — and RadiologyExam.contrastRequired exists. The two facts sit in the same database and nothing brings them together. The only pregnancyRelated field in the whole schema belongs to DeathCertificate.
findings.proof: read from the schema and confirmed against a live patient record

findings.title: consultationId is not tenant-checked
findings.detail: Order creation guards the patient and the exam with isOwned, but consultationId passes from the body into the row unchecked.
findings.proof: read from the controller

findings.title: Every search returned 400 — three columns did not exist
findings.detail: The shared helper was called with relation: null, injecting Patient's five searchable columns onto PreTriage itself. A PreTriage row is a walk-in who is not a patient yet: it has firstName, lastName and phone, never middleName, mrn or phonePrimary. Both the count and the findMany failed, so the list and all four stat cards went together. Live since 5 August, from commit d09c061.
findings.proof: FIXED and verified: /pre-triage?search=r now 200 with 10 rows; combined with status=routed also 200

findings.title: The search is not debounced
findings.detail: Three characters typed at 60 ms produced two requests, plus one refetch with nothing changed — a useEffect dependency. src/lib/useDebounce.js already solves this.
findings.proof: measured, e2e/audit-report/live/f-pre-triage.log

findings.title: Both icon-only buttons have no accessible name
findings.detail: The eye and the pencil have no text, no aria-label and no title. Nameable only from the lucide class on their svg — which is why a screen reader cannot use them.
findings.proof: Lighthouse accessibility 89; discovery could only name them by DOM position

findings.title: Every search returned 400 — causeOfDeath is not a column
findings.detail: The statutory form stores the cause as a chain of four: immediateCause (a), antecedentCauseB, C, D. Searching a non-existent causeOfDeath made both the count and the findMany fail from the first keystroke. Live since 5 August, from commit d09c061.
findings.proof: FIXED and verified: /death-certificates?search=ra now 200 with 3 rows; with place=inpatient, 200 with 2 rows

findings.title: Not yet checked — numbering, re-issue, and who certifies
findings.detail: Whether the certificate number is minted per organisation (Day Care and Death Certificates have shared one series before), whether an issued certificate can be re-issued, and whether certifiedById is taken from the body as it is in Radiology.
findings.proof: open question, not measured

findings.title: limit=500 is a cap, not pagination — 667 KB
findings.detail: /api/patients?status=active&limit=500 returns 667 KB. With 200,000 patients, everything past the five-hundredth is silently invisible. This is the same defect that once made 99.99% of patients unfindable when raising a death certificate.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: Each patient card fetches its records separately — up to 1,717 ms
findings.detail: Opening cards one at a time issues a fresh /patients/{id}/records per card. One took 1,717 ms in the live log.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: Coverage 96% — one combobox unreachable
findings.detail: 40 controls found, 27 clicked, nothing left unexplained. Nine were tel: links to patients' own phone numbers, which leave the app and can never be part of coverage; two are write buttons and one is destructive. The single miss is a combobox the page re-rendered away from before the click landed.
findings.proof: measured 9 August, e2e/audit-report/live/f-patients.log — Lighthouse 44/89

findings.title: limit=2000 returns 950 KB
findings.detail: /api/laboratory?resource=tests&limit=2000 is the single largest response in the application. Two more on the same screen use limit=2000 for orders and results.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: LaboratoryModule.jsx is 2,479 lines — the largest file in the repository
findings.detail: Three transforms, three zod schemas, four lookup tables, five tabs of UI, six dialogs and eight API handlers in one file. The print template was already extracted to printLabReport.js after the same report had been written twice; the rest has not been.
findings.proof: wc -l, and the duplication scan

findings.title: The bed race holds — two admissions, one bed, one wins
findings.detail: Compare-and-set is correct: the bed's expected status is part of the where clause, so the second writer matches zero rows and gets a 409. Recorded because the equivalent check in Queue DID fail and had to be rewritten.
findings.proof: backend/scripts/ipd-bed-race.mjs — call A 201, call B 409 IPD_BED_UNAVAILABLE

findings.title: Eleven controls navigate out of the module
findings.detail: Six land on the Dashboard rather than the screen their label promises — including “Triage Patient” and “Lab Order”. “New Invoice” goes to Billing, “Book Appointment” to Appointments.
findings.proof: measured — the walk recorded each one and returned

findings.title: Not yet checked — discharge, charges and bed-board scoping
findings.detail: Whether discharge frees the bed atomically, whether IpdCharge totals are recomputed server-side, and whether the bed board is org-scoped on every read.
findings.proof: open question, not measured

findings.title: Module on/off switches have no accessible name
findings.detail: Each switch is a button with no text, no aria-label, no title and no icon class. A screen reader cannot use it — and neither could the audit, which pressed all fifteen and disabled fifteen modules of a running system.
findings.proof: the audit's own PATCH log: modulesEnabled {patients:false, …}

findings.title: A disabled module silently renders the Dashboard
findings.detail: The route is filtered out of the router and falls through to the catch-all. The URL quietly changes to /admin and nothing tells the user the module is switched off — they will report it as missing.
findings.proof: e2e/route-check.mjs — 12 of 16 routes did this while modules were off

findings.title: /api/settings?resource=users returns 319 KB and is called by five modules
findings.detail: Appointments, Inpatient, Day Care, Doctor Accountability and Register all pull it. An earlier pass took it from 1,698 KB to 312 KB with an explicit select; it is still the third-largest response in the app.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: limit=1000 returns 536 KB
findings.detail: /api/appointments?limit=1000&status=scheduled,confirmed,checked_in,in_progress. Three call sites use limit=1000; Today and Doctor Slots have no pagination at all, only a “showing N of M” banner.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: The Weekly view issues one request per day — seven of 54 KB each
findings.detail: Roughly 380 KB to render one week, and the same again when the week changes. /appointments/calendar-counts already returns a whole month in 2 KB.
findings.proof: measured from the live API log

findings.title: A Weekly appointment chip looks clickable and is not
findings.detail: cursor-pointer with no onClick in WeeklyView.jsx. Reschedule also shows 24-hour times while the rest of the module shows 12-hour.
findings.proof: read from the code, confirmed by the walk's no-handler check

findings.title: Catalogue pricing is correct — the server prices every line
findings.detail: A request carrying its own unitPrice is ignored; lib/catalogPrice.js looks the price up server-side. Recorded because the counter multiplying a client-supplied price is a bug this repo has already paid for.
findings.proof: backend/scripts/billing-money-probe.mjs

findings.title: Not yet checked — the money paths
findings.detail: Invoice-number collision under concurrency, payment against a cancelled invoice, refunding twice, refunding more than was paid, and the fulfilment cascade (billing a test raises the lab order and draws down pharmacy stock inside the invoice transaction). Probes are written; none has been run.
findings.proof: open question, not measured

findings.title: Two counters pressing Call Next got the same patient
findings.detail: The read-then-write was not atomic. Now a compare-and-set claims the row, retries up to five times, and returns a 409 the counter can act on rather than a silent double-call.
findings.proof: backend/scripts/queue-race.mjs — reproduced before, refused after

findings.title: The queue token used the server's date, not the hospital's
findings.detail: After 6:30 pm IST the token carried tomorrow's date, so the first patient of the evening got a number from the next day's series.
findings.proof: backend/src/utils/queueNumber.js now uses ymdInZone

findings.title: Choosing one dropdown value re-renders the form 177 times
findings.detail: Opening the New Screening dialog and picking a value fires Controller 177 times in one commit (97 ms), and 142 times on the next. react-hook-form is re-rendering every field on the form, not the one that changed — the cost grows with each field added to the screening form.
findings.proof: React profiler during the walk — dialog combobox click, e2e/audit-report/live/f-pre-triage.log

findings.title: Closing the dialog costs 302 ms of render
findings.detail: Routes 302.7ms ×3 when the New Screening dialog is dismissed — the whole route tree re-renders to close an overlay.
findings.proof: React profiler during the walk

findings.title: The date filter is correct — all six options carry the range
findings.detail: Today, This Week, This Month, Specific Date, Custom Range and the All Dates reset were each exercised. The query string carries startDate and endDate every time, in hospital-timezone form. The three that returned zero rows returned zero honestly — the seeded screenings are June and July records, not August.
findings.proof: measured: ?startDate=2026-08-09&endDate=2026-08-09 etc.

findings.title: Page load is light — 4 requests, 15.1 KB, no limit over three digits
findings.detail: /auth/me 0.1 KB, /settings 6.4 KB, /pre-triage?page=1&limit=10 8.5 KB. No rule 5 violation, no duplicate call, zero console errors and zero 4xx/5xx across the whole walk.
findings.proof: measured 9 August after the search fix — previously this module produced 19 critical events, all of them the 400

findings.title: Opening a row refetches the whole list AND loses the date filter
findings.detail: Page load asks for today: /queue?startDate=2026-08-09&endDate=2026-08-09&page=1&limit=10. Clicking a row to expand it fires /queue?page=1&limit=10 — 9.6 KB, ten rows, and no date range at all. The list silently stops being today's queue and becomes every queue entry ever, without the user touching the filter. Expanding a row should not refetch the list; refetching it without the filter that produced it is the part that changes what the counter is looking at.
findings.proof: measured — page load carried startDate/endDate, every row click did not. e2e/audit-report/live/f-queue.log

findings.title: Every other row click costs 110–175 ms and a 9.6 KB refetch
findings.detail: Rows alternate 1 request / 0 requests — expanding fetches, collapsing does not. Eight expansions in the walk cost eight full list fetches. On a ward counter opening rows to read details, that is a 9.6 KB round trip per glance.
findings.proof: measured: 158 ms, 110 ms, 115 ms, 175 ms, 150 ms across consecutive row clicks

findings.title: One row click re-renders 340 elements for 622 ms
findings.detail: Primitive.div 622.7ms ×340 on a single row expansion — higher than any other module measured so far (Pre-Triage's worst was 177). The whole table re-renders to open one row.
findings.proof: React profiler during the walk

findings.title: Page load is light — 4 requests, 16 KB, and the date filter IS applied
findings.detail: /auth/me, /settings and one /queue call scoped to today. 64 controls discovered — 39 buttons, 11 filters, 3 tabs, 10 rows, and no icon-only buttons at all, which is why this module has no accessible-name findings. The slowest thing on load is React, not the network: Routes 441.9ms ×36.
findings.proof: measured 9 August

findings.title: A month date-range takes 3.8 seconds to return ten rows
findings.detail:
/queue?startDate=2026-08-01&endDate=2026-08-31&page=1&limit=10 — 3,793 ms for 9.5 KB and ten rows. A week takes 1,280 ms. A tiny answer that takes that long is a query problem, not a payload one: the date range is being scanned rather than indexed. On Render, with real network latency and a cold connection, this is the difference between a counter working and a counter waiting.

Re-verified 10 August. Queue, month range: re-measured as a median of 163 ms (runs 78/163/3,501). The original was a single cold-pool sample. See PERF-REVERIFY.
findings.proof: measured — 3793 ms (month), 1280 ms (week), 905 ms (unfiltered). e2e/audit-report/live/f-queue.log

findings.title: WITHDRAWN — "one action re-renders 1,009 elements for 6.7 seconds"
findings.detail:
This was reported as the worst single render in the application. It was the worst single measurement error instead.

Retracted 10 August — measuring error. This count came from e2e/profiler.mjs, which counted every fiber whose actualDuration was above zero. React leaves that value on a fiber after its last render, so a component that bailed out of a commit still carried the cost of whenever it did render, and the walk counted it again on every commit. The tool now compares actualStartTime against the end of the previous commit and reports self time with children subtracted. Re-measured on Queue — the module with the largest number here — three keystrokes produce App ×16 and Navigation ×16, and no NavLink renders at all: the memoisation in src/App.jsx (commit 15c804d) is working. The shell does still re-render once per commit, which is worth its own look, but it is not the hundreds this row claimed.

Re-measured on the same action — typing three characters into the queue search — the heaviest component was SelectItem at 44 ms of self time, not 6,742. The real defect underneath it was genuine and is recorded as QUEUE-ROWMEMO below: every row rebuilt its five-option priority <Select> on each keystroke.
findings.proof: retracted 10 August after fixing e2e/profiler.mjs; re-measured worst self time 44 ms
findings.retraction: the number was the measuring tool, not the application

findings.title: 99 refetches of /queue in one walk
findings.detail: The same /queue?page=1&limit=10 request fired 99 times while walking the module — on row expansions, on tab switches, and on actions with nothing to do with the queue list. At 9.6 KB each that is roughly 950 KB of repeated payload for one session.
findings.proof: counted from the run log

findings.title: The Queue module imports the whole Billing module
findings.detail: QueueModule.jsx:14 imports BillingModule directly and renders it inside a tab (:269). Billing is 1,986 lines. Every user who opens Queue downloads and mounts Billing whether they touch that tab or not — and the walk correctly found seven tabs under Queue, four of which are Billing's own. CLAUDE.md rule 10 asks for exactly the opposite: a module should arrive as its own chunk behind React.lazy.
findings.proof: read from the source, and confirmed by the walk discovering Billing's tabs and invoice rows under Queue

findings.title: WITHDRAWN — "the search box fires nothing at all"
findings.detail:
Re-measured against the running app: typing eight characters into "Search patient or invoice #" at 60 ms produced exactly one request, carrying search=INV-2026 in the query string. The box works and is debounced.

The original reading came from the walk typing into a search input on a tab where the list is filtered in the browser (Insurance claims are fetched in full and narrowed client-side, BillingModule.jsx:1109), so no request was correct behaviour there. The finding described one box and was written as if it described the module.
findings.proof: retracted 10 August — re-measured in a real browser: 8 chars typed, 1 request, /billing?resource=invoices&limit=10&offset=0&search=INV-2026

findings.title: 91-94% of the CSS on every page is never used — ~158 KB each time
findings.detail:
Measured against the production build with the DevTools Coverage panel: every page downloads 172 KB of CSS and uses between 10 and 15 KB of it. Dashboard uses 10 KB, Laboratory 15 KB, Queue 11 KB. The remaining ~158 KB is downloaded, parsed and thrown away on every single page, for every user. That is the signature of Tailwind's purge not reaching the files it should — the whole utility set is shipping instead of the classes actually used.

This is the one number here that is absolute: it comes from the built bundle, it is a separate file from the JavaScript, and minification does not distort it.
findings.proof: node e2e/devtools-extra.mjs against `vite preview` — 172 KB loaded / 10-15 KB used across all eight modules measured

findings.title: Queue loads 950 KB more JavaScript than Billing does — because it contains Billing
findings.detail:
Coverage, measured per module: queue 3,071 KB · billing 2,121 KB · laboratory 2,369 KB · dashboard 1,464 KB. Queue is the heaviest module in the application and carries roughly 950 KB more than Billing itself. The cause was found by reading the code — QueueModule.jsx:14 imports BillingModule directly and renders it in a tab — and this is the measurement that confirms it. A receptionist who only ever watches the queue still downloads and mounts the entire billing module.

Read this as a comparison between modules, not as what a user downloads. It was taken against the dev server, where each file is served separately with its HMR wrapper, because the production build is minified and V8 then reports almost everything as used. Dev gives an honest ranking; only the CSS figure above is an honest absolute.
findings.proof: node e2e/devtools-extra.mjs — JS coverage per module, plus QueueModule.jsx:14 and :269

findings.title: The session token is in localStorage AND in an HttpOnly cookie
findings.detail:
The Application panel shows the same JWT in two places: a cookie marked HttpOnly — which is correct, JavaScript cannot read it — and a token key in localStorage, which any script running on the page can read with one line.

Holding it in both cancels the protection the cookie provides. The point of HttpOnly is that a script injected through any route — a dependency, a stored value rendered as HTML, a browser extension — cannot reach the session. With the token also in localStorage, it can.

The cookie also carries no Secure flag, so it will be sent over plain HTTP.
findings.proof: node e2e/devtools-extra.mjs — Application panel: localStorage key `token` matches the JWT shape; cookie `token` HttpOnly · no Secure · SameSite=Lax

findings.title: The heap does not quite return to where it started
findings.detail:
Each module was loaded, left, and garbage-collected before the heap was read. On the page the heap sits at 20-25 MB; after leaving it falls back to about 9.4 MB — so nothing large is being held. But the floor drifts upward across the eight modules: 9,426 → 9,446 → 9,454 → 9,514 → 9,561 → 9,550 KB, about 124 KB not reclaimed over eight navigations.

This is not a leak in the usual sense; a leak would be megabytes. It matters because of who uses this app: a counter that keeps one browser tab open all day, moving between modules hundreds of times. One reading is noise — the drift is the signal, and it needs a longer run to confirm.
findings.proof: node e2e/devtools-extra.mjs — Runtime.getHeapUsage after HeapProfiler.collectGarbage, per module

findings.title: Precise JavaScript coverage of the SHIPPED bundle is still not measured
findings.detail:
Two attempts produced numbers that could not be true. The first summed V8's nested ranges and reported more bytes used than loaded — impossible, and the giveaway. That is fixed. The second ran against the production build and reported 0% waste for every module, which is an artefact of minification: the whole file collapses into a few large functions, and V8 marks a function used the moment it runs once.

So the JS figures in this report are from the dev server and are comparative only. Getting an honest absolute needs source maps applied to the built bundle. Recorded here rather than left as a number nobody should trust.

findings.title: There was no way to ask what was billed today
findings.detail:
Invoices could be narrowed by search, status and type — never by date. The one question a counter asks every evening had no control at all, and the backend did not read startDate/endDate either.

It now reuses useDateFilter, the control Patients, Pre-Triage and Queue already share, and filters in the DATABASE: a page-local filter would only ever search the ten rows on screen and would report "no invoices in March" while March sat on page four.

Two details that decide whether it is right: dayRange resolves the day in the hospital's timezone, so a bill raised after 18:30 IST does not fall into tomorrow; and an empty range is not assigned at all, because invoiceDate: {} matches nothing in Prisma and a blank filter would have returned zero invoices instead of all.
findings.proof: backend/scripts/billing-filter-matrix.mjs — all 16 filter combinations, 0 problems, plus four date checks including that an invoice is found on its IST day

findings.title: The New Invoice catalogues are capped at 500 rows — 1,079 KB, and the rest is invisible
findings.detail:
Choosing a department on the New Invoice tab pulls that catalogue with limit=500: /laboratory?resource=tests 287.3 KB / 500 rows, /radiology?resource=exams 196.8 KB / 500 rows, /pharmacy/drugs 595.0 KB / 500 rows — 1,079 KB across the three. The pharmacy catalogue is roughly 200,000 rows, so a cashier can reach 0.25% of it and the other 99.75% reports as "no results" for drugs that exist. This is rule 5: a cap is not pagination, and rows past it vanish with no message.

One correction to how this was first described: the three do not load together when the tab opens. Each fires only when its department is selected, so a single bill costs one of the three, not all 1,079 KB. The cap is the defect; the bundling was not real.
findings.proof: measured 10 August, e2e/verify-billing-claims.mjs — laboratory 287.3 KB/500 rows, radiology 196.8 KB/500 rows, pharmacy 595.0 KB/500 rows; the New Invoice tab itself fired 0 catalogue calls

findings.title: Every keystroke, filter and clear fires four requests where one is needed
findings.detail:
Three actions were measured and all three behave the same way. Typing INV into the invoice search fired four requests and only one carried the search term; the other three — ?resource=services, ?resource=stats and /insurance — re-read data no user input had touched. Clearing the search: four again. Changing the status filter: four again.

The cause is one effect at BillingModule.jsx:622-629. fetchAll bundles four fetchers, and fetchBills closes over page, search, status, type and date — so its identity changes on every interaction, which changes fetchAll, which re-runs the effect, which calls all four. The other three depend on none of it.

This is the measured, per-request form of the vaguer "queries refetch when nothing has changed" already recorded against this module.
findings.proof: measured 10 August, e2e/verify-billing-claims.mjs — search "INV": 4 requests, 1 carried search=; clear: 4 requests, 1 useful; status filter: 4 requests, 1 carried status=paid

findings.title: Not proved either way — whether paging fires the same four requests

It was not measured at all: the status filter applied a step earlier had narrowed the list to a single row, so Next was disabled and never clicked. Zero requests from a control that was never pressed is a broken test, not a passing one.

Given the cause recorded in BI9 lives in a shared effect and fetchBills closes over invoicesPage, paging almost certainly fires the same four — but "almost certainly" is not a measurement, and this row stays open until one exists.

findings.title: FIXED — Queue downloaded Billing and Appointments for a receptionist who opened neither
findings.detail:
QueueModule.jsx imported BillingModule and AppointmentsModule statically to render them in two of its tabs. Radix unmounts an inactive TabsContent, so neither ever mounted — the bytes were downloaded and parsed for nothing, on the one screen a hospital leaves open all day.

Both are now behind lazy() with a named <Suspense> fallback, so the tab says "Loading Billing…" rather than nothing while the chunk arrives.

findings.title: FIXED — every queue row rebuilt a five-option Select on each keystroke
findings.detail:
Each QueueRow carries its own priority <Select>. The row was not memoised and the module's three row handlers were rebuilt on every render, so typing one character into the queue search — which the rows do not read — re-rendered all ten rows and all fifty options.

QueueRow is now memo'd and callNext, setStatus and changePriority are useCallback'd. The second half is what makes the first half work: memo compares props by reference, so a handler rebuilt each render would have defeated it silently while looking like it had been fixed.
findings.proof: measured 10 August — typing "ram": SelectItem renders 722 → 356 (51% fewer), QueueRow renders 97 → 47 (52% fewer)

findings.title: FIXED — the 429 KB spreadsheet parser loaded for everyone who opened Laboratory
findings.detail:
BulkImportDialog pulls in xlsx, the heaviest dependency in the application, and it exists so an administrator can occasionally import a catalogue. It was imported statically by both Laboratory and Radiology, so every visitor paid for it on page load.

It is now lazy() and gated on showImport. The gate is the part that matters: a lazy component fetches its chunk the moment it renders, and this dialog was rendered on every page with open={false} — so lazy() alone would have changed nothing while appearing to fix it.
findings.proof: measured 10 August — Laboratory route JS 1,519 KB → 1,203 KB, of which xlsx 850 KB → 0 KB. Verified the dialog still opens with its content in both modules (e2e/smoke-lazy.mjs).

findings.title: The profiler was counting components that had not re-rendered
findings.detail: Recorded as a finding against the tooling, because it is the reason a number in this report was wrong and every render count in it was inflated. e2e/profiler.mjs counted any fiber with actualDuration > 0; React leaves that value in place after a render, so untouched components were counted on every commit. /pharmacy/stats 1,204 ms → 226 ms (runs 211/226/228)

Pharmacy, Primitive.div: 2,254 ms → 6.5 ms (worst is now PharmacyModule at 100 ms, which is a real and separate thing to look at)
